introduction_markdown:
Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board, Ordinary Level Examination, June 2020. Chemistry, Paper 2 (subject code 0515). Duration: two and a half hours.

This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: attempt ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 questions answered. Section B: answer BOTH questions in this section. Section C: answer 2 questions out of 3.

In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Non-programmable calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** relative atomic masses H = 1.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0, Cu = 64.0; 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g$^{-1}$ $^\circ$C$^{-1}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^\circ$C = 273 K.

questions.enonce_markdown: Chemical reduction: choose a suitable example and describe how the metal is extracted from its ore. *[8 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Example: iron**, extracted from **haematite**, $\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}$, in the **blast furnace**.

- The furnace is charged from the top with the ore, **coke** (carbon) and **limestone**; hot air is blown in near the bottom.
- Coke burns in the hot air: $\mathrm{C} + \mathrm{O_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{CO_2}$ (this heats the furnace).
- Carbon dioxide is reduced by more coke: $\mathrm{CO_2} + \mathrm{C} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO}$.
- Carbon monoxide is the reducing agent: $\mathrm{Fe_2O_3} + 3\mathrm{CO} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Fe} + 3\mathrm{CO_2}$.
- Limestone removes the sand (silicon dioxide) impurity: $\mathrm{CaCO_3} \rightarrow \mathrm{CaO} + \mathrm{CO_2}$, then $\mathrm{CaO} + \mathrm{SiO_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{CaSiO_3}$ (slag).
- Molten iron sinks to the bottom, with the lighter molten slag floating on top; both are tapped off separately.

(Balance check: $\mathrm{Fe_2O_3} + 3\mathrm{CO}$: Fe 2, C 3, O 6 on each side.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Electrolytic reduction: choose a suitable example and describe how the metal is extracted from its ore. *[8 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Example: aluminium**, extracted from **bauxite**.

- Bauxite is first purified to pure **aluminium oxide (alumina)**, $\mathrm{Al_2O_3}$.
- Alumina has a very high melting point (about $2000\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$), so it is **dissolved in molten cryolite**, $\mathrm{Na_3AlF_6}$, which lowers the working temperature to about $900$ to $1000\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and improves the conductivity.
- The molten mixture is electrolysed in a steel tank lined with graphite, which is the **cathode**; **graphite (carbon) blocks** are the **anodes**.
- Cathode: $\mathrm{Al^{3+}} + 3e^- \rightarrow \mathrm{Al}$ (molten aluminium collects at the bottom and is tapped off).
- Anode: $2\mathrm{O^{2-}} \rightarrow \mathrm{O_2} + 4e^-$; the oxygen burns the anodes: $\mathrm{C} + \mathrm{O_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{CO_2}$, so the anodes must be replaced regularly.
- Overall: $2\mathrm{Al_2O_3} \rightarrow 4\mathrm{Al} + 3\mathrm{O_2}$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Give two large scale uses of each metal. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
- **Iron** (mostly as steel): construction (girders, bridges, reinforcing rods) and making car bodies, machinery, ships, railway lines.
- **Aluminium:** overhead electric power cables (light, good conductor) and aircraft bodies; also cooking pots, drink cans and food-wrapping foil.
